saints.name: St. John Climacus
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: The abbot of Mount Sinai whose “Ladder of Divine Ascent” has guided monks and pilgrims toward God for centuries…
biography: Born about 579, John came as a youth to the monastery of Mount Sinai, the present St. Catherine's, and was formed in the monastic life by an elder named Martyrius. After his master's death he withdrew to a hermitage at the foot of the mountain, where he spent long years in solitude, studying the lives of the saints.

When he was about sixty-five the monks persuaded him to be their abbot. At the request of John, abbot of Raithu on the Red Sea, he wrote the work from which he takes his surname: the Klimax, or Ladder of Divine Ascent, which pictures the soul's climb to God in thirty steps, answering to the thirty years of Christ's hidden life. A shorter companion treatise, To the Pastor, also survives.

The Ladder became one of the most beloved books of Byzantine spirituality and is read to this day in Orthodox monasteries during Great Lent, whose fourth Sunday is dedicated to him. He died about 649, and East and West alike keep his feast on 30 March.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 30 March
